pr.title: The transport arrives: field plays live on Windows over a named pipe (windows-portability.md chunks 4-5)
pr.head: 6a529d185f7d7907f1cc808df31c4095648403e9

summary: field-audiod is the native audio daemon. The CLI spawns it on demand for each project, talks to it over a control channel that carries newline-delimited JSON requests and broadcast events, and the daemon exits on its own when idle. On macOS and Linux that channel is a Unix domain socket at .field/audiod.sock. Node cannot open a Unix socket on Windows, and the daemon's socket code was POSIX-only, so until this change field play, field transport and live rendering could not run on Windows at all.

This pull request gives Windows its own transport: a named pipe, the Windows local IPC object that Node dials natively. The CLI derives the pipe's name from the project root and hands it to the daemon with --socket, so both ends use one string. In the daemon, request handling moves above the I/O layer and is shared by both platforms. Only accepting, reading, writing and shutting down split per platform, and the POSIX arm moves unchanged.

Two small pieces of the same plan ride along: field play without a built daemon now refuses the afplay fallback on every platform except macOS, and CI gains a windows-latest job. The tests that were skipped on Windows until the transport existed run there now. The Python generation workers keep their POSIX transport, which is a later chunk of the plan.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Named pipe: Windows local IPC, addressed as \\.\pipe\name. A server creates instances, and each client connection uses one instance.
  • Parked instance: the one instance the daemon keeps ready for the next client.
  • ConnectNamedPipe: the server call that waits for a client on an instance. With overlapped (asynchronous) I/O it returns at once and completes later through an OVERLAPPED record and an event.
  • FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE: makes instance creation fail if the name already exists, which gives the one-owner guarantee.
  • CancelIoEx: cancels the I/O pending on a handle at that moment. Later I/O is unaffected.
  • SHUT_RD: the POSIX half-close the socket arm uses. Every later read returns end-of-file.
  • Idle exit: the daemon quits when no client is connected, nothing plays, and it has been quiet for the idle period.
  • MessageManagerLock: JUCE's lock on the daemon's message thread. Every request but session takes it.

cards.title: Review history so far
cards.html:
• The author's own reviews on a63ec97 found an OVERLAPPED record the kernel could write after its stack frame was gone, on the ordinary shutdown path. It is fixed: every accept iteration now reaps a pending connect before it exits.
  • The afplay guard widened from Windows to every non-macOS platform after #162's review, and the plan's §2.2 records why.
  • Projector's review on 1eff8a0 found that field play still announces the afplay fallback before refusing it. That thread is still open.
  • Projector's review on 6a529d1 opened four threads: an accept-loop spin, the pipe's access rights, docs/architecture.md left behind, and the CI comments. It reviewed by reading only, because the author has no write access to the repository.

groups.title: The pipe name both ends agree on
groups.kicker: How the CLI names a project's pipe and tells the daemon
intro: Every command that reaches the daemon asks socketPathFor where it is. On POSIX the answer stays a path relative to the current directory, which keeps it inside the 104-byte limit on socket paths. On Windows the function now returns a pipe name instead: field- followed by 24 hex characters of a SHA-256 over the resolved project root, lowercased, and the socket's relative path. Lowercasing matters because NTFS compares paths without regard to case, and two spellings of one root must reach one daemon.
When the CLI has to spawn the daemon, it passes the same string with --socket. POSIX keeps passing the relative path, which the daemon binds against its working directory, the project root.

checks.text: Every caller of socketPathFor hands the result to net.connect or server.listen, except helloIfRunning in src/commands/version.ts, which first calls existsSync on it. That file is not in this diff, but on Windows the check now stats a pipe name, and Node's existsSync stats by opening the path. The accept-loop finding in the next group names this as one way a client opens and closes the pipe.

files.note: The Windows branch of socketPathFor: a hashed pipe name per project root and socket.

checks.text: Lowercasing covers case only. An 8.3 short name, a subst drive or a junction is another spelling of the same root and hashes to a different pipe. The review lists hashing realpathSync.native(root) as a suggestion.

files.note: The spawn passes the full pipe name on Windows and the relative socket path elsewhere.

checks.text: path here is the same value tryConnect dials, so on Windows the daemon binds exactly the name the client opens.

groups.title: The daemon's Windows transport
groups.kicker: Shared request handling above, a named-pipe accept, read and shutdown loop below
intro: server.cpp now has one copy of request handling for both platforms: handleLine parses a line, dispatch runs the operation, and broadcast sends an event to every open connection. Below that, an #if defined(_WIN32) arm implements the destructor, start, acceptLoop, readLoop, send, beginShutdown and sweepClosedConnections with Win32 handles. The #else arm is the POSIX code, moved as it was.

start creates the first pipe instance with FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE, so a second daemon for the same project fails there. acceptLoop then runs one overlapped ConnectNamedPipe at a time on the parked instance. It polls every 200 ms rather than waiting forever, because the shutdown wake-up can be lost. When a client arrives, the loop parks a fresh instance, hands the connected one to a new reader thread, and goes round again.

The POSIX arm half-closes each socket with SHUT_RD, so readers see end-of-file and the drain loop in main.cpp can finish. Windows has no such state. beginShutdown uses CancelIoEx to cancel each pending read, and readLoop checks running each cycle so it does not start a fresh read and serve a busy client forever. After the loop, a reader drains exactly the bytes buffered at that moment, which matches what SHUT_RD still delivers.

checks.text: The POSIX arm and the shared request handling match the base: the review extracted both halves from windows/build and this head and diffed them. The only differences are blank lines and the processId() helper that replaces ::getpid() in hello.

No Windows code here was compiled or run during the review, because the head is untrusted. The pull request body reports 8/8 protocol tests, 12/12 play-daemon tests and 25+1 hosting tests passing on Windows hardware.

files.note: Shared request handling, then the Windows arm (accept, read, write, shutdown on pipe handles), then the POSIX arm unchanged.

checks.text: Every local account can read the daemon's pipe, and remote clients are accepted. Both CreateNamedPipeA calls pass nullptr security attributes, whose default grants read access to Everyone and the anonymous account, and leave out PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS. Another account can open the pipe read-only, receive every broadcast, and keep the idle exit from firing. Plan §2.1 chose pipes because their ACLs would match the 0600 Unix socket. Fix: a DACL for the current user only, and PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS in both calls.
The bounded poll. A SetEvent from beginShutdown can land before the ResetEvent at the top of the iteration and be lost, so the loop re-reads running every 200 ms.

Every exit from an accept iteration with a connect still pending passes this block, which cancels the connect and waits for the kernel to finish with ov before the stack frame ends. The review traced the break, the continue and the accept path.

A client that hangs up before ConnectNamedPipe leaves this loop spinning forever. ConnectNamedPipe then fails with ERROR_NO_DATA until the server calls DisconnectNamedPipe, and this continue retries the same handle. While it spins, no client can connect until the idle exit, which never fires during playback. Fix: call DisconnectNamedPipe (pipe) before the continue.

The review's suggestions note a narrower gap here. A read issued after beginShutdown's CancelIoEx is never cancelled, so a client that goes quiet just then keeps the drain waiting. Re-checking running once the read is pending closes it.
The shutdown drain peeks once and reads exactly that many bytes, because peeking again would follow a client that keeps writing.

files.note: Connection and Server state split per platform: a pipe handle, the parked instance and the accept event on Windows; the descriptors and the lock on POSIX.

groups.title: No afplay fallback off macOS
groups.kicker: field play without a built daemon refuses on Windows and Linux
intro: Without a built daemon, field play on macOS falls back to playing artifacts through afplay, a macOS command. On any other platform that spawn could only fail with an error that names a tool the machine never had. playWithAfplay now throws the build hint first. Plan §2.2 decides there is no Windows fallback, and its amendment widens that to every platform but macOS.

files.note: The platform guard at the top of playWithAfplay, and the comment above it.

checks.text: The caller still announces the fallback it is about to refuse. Line 746 prints "field-audiod is not built; using afplay" unconditionally, and then playWithAfplay throws "the afplay fallback is macOS-only". Fix: move the platform test up to the !daemonBinary() branch, beside the refusal for --from and the other daemon-only flags.

groups.title: Tests that run on Windows now
groups.kicker: Retired skip guards, platform-neutral assertions, and a cleanup that waits for the daemon
intro: Until the transport existed, every test that dialed the daemon or faked one was skipped on Windows. Those guards come off here: the protocol, play-daemon and live-session suites, the live plugin-hosting chains, and the nine fake-daemon tests in version.test.ts, whose fakes now listen on whatever socketPathFor returns.

One Windows behaviour needed a helper. Windows cannot delete a directory that is a live process's working directory, and the daemon takes a few hundred milliseconds to exit after quit. removeTempProject in src/testing/temp.ts retries the whole removal for up to ten seconds, and returns on its first try on POSIX. The commit at this head also ports the click, punch and record daemon tests to it, and skips the POSIX mode-bit asserts in the credentials test on Windows.

checks.text: Each test file that drops an rmSync call still uses rmSync elsewhere or no longer imports it. The repository's tsconfig.json sets noUnusedLocals, so a stale import would fail pnpm typecheck. Checked by grep at this head.

files.note: New helper: retries a recursive delete for up to ten seconds while a daemon exits.

checks.text: The fake daemon is a Node pipe server on Windows. Node keeps several instances listening, unlike the real daemon's one parked instance, so these tests cannot exercise the accept-loop behaviour in server.cpp.

groups.title: The Windows CI job and the plan's record
groups.kicker: A windows-latest job, and windows-portability.md marking chunks 4 and 5 implemented
intro: The new windows job runs what the Linux job runs, except the Python type checks, because the workers stay on their POSIX transport. It has not run on a runner yet: the pull request body says the account's Actions billing currently starts no jobs.

The plan records chunk 4 and chunk 5 as implemented, amends §2.2 to cover every platform but macOS, and answers two of its §6 open questions. A third is mostly answered: one manual test, a physical unplug during playback, stays open. The plan stays at in-progress.

checks.text: The workflow's comments say CI is one Linux job and that this key adds the OS. The header at line 8 still opens "One job, on Linux" and argues cost from runner rates, though Windows minutes bill at twice the Linux rate. The Linux key at line 70 already includes runner.os, so the two keys are the same. Fix: rewrite the header for both jobs, and describe this key as the Linux key.

files.note: Chunk 4 and 5 records, the §2.2 amendment, and three §6 answers.

checks.text: docs/architecture.md still says the daemon uses a Unix socket and a lock file, at lines 81 and 164. AGENTS.md § Docs says a change that moves behaviour and leaves docs/ behind is unfinished. Fix: say in both passages that on Windows field-audiod listens on a named pipe owned through FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE.
This chunk 5 record says playWithAfplay fails "on win32", but the §2.2 amendment at line 258 and the code both refuse on every platform except macOS.
